narrative.overview: The site is the quick-start card that should have shipped inside the pedal's box: cool paper stock, one dark ink, one signal orange, and a grid of switches printed like a technical sheet. It treats the visitor as someone about to plug hardware in, not someone browsing a SaaS landing page. The documentation keeps the same inks but lowers its voice: a reading surface with tabular data, hairline rules and terminal captures as evidence.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper gray and ink, with one signal orange doing all the pointing.
A 4x4 switch matrix that doubles as the documentation index.
Condensed technical labels in mono; sentences in a grotesk.
Terminal captures framed as evidence, never as decoration.
Flat surfaces, hairline borders, almost no radius.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Orange marks what is live, selected or clickable. It never fills a large region and never appears twice in the same glance for two different meanings.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: Explanations live on paper; device output lives on terminal black. Never mix the two inside one component.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Mono Rule
rules.body: CC values, addresses, modes, commands and byte counts are set in Spline Sans Mono. Prose is never monospaced for flavor.

dos: Keep one orange meaning per view: the live switch, the install prompt or a primary link.
Set every address, mode byte and command in Spline Sans Mono.
Put real terminal captures on terminal black and explain them in paper-coloured prose.
Keep the switch matrix as the navigation; it is the product's own structure.
donts: Add rounded cards, gradient text, glass panels or colored left borders.
Use the green outside a connection state.
Invent screenshots, testimonials, benchmarks or claims the hardware notes do not support.
Let motion hide content: every entrance must end visible, and reduced motion must show the final state immediately.
